raw: **Pattern 1: The Solo Reasoner** — Single-agent ReAct loop for focused intelligence tasks[^143]
teaching_note: The Focused Analytic Reasoner answers one bounded question by alternating proposed steps and authorized observations; it is not a free-ranging collector. ReAct is an architecture and task-scoped research result, not a general factual-reliability guarantee; use the shared claim record in Section [@sec:analytic-workflow]. [@scholarly_yao_2023_react]
title: Pattern 1: The Solo Reasoner — Single-agent ReAct loop for focused intelligence tasks

raw: *Methods*: Chain-of-Thought, Self-Critique, Reflection Scoring
teaching_note: Record an inspectable trace: question → source passage → short rationale → proposed local read → permission decision → returned passage → conclusion or abstention. Do not require private hidden reasoning or treat an internal reflection score as evidence; absence of support and exhaustion of the two-read classroom budget are stopping conditions.
title: Methods: Chain-of-Thought, Self-Critique, Reflection Scoring

raw: *Application*: Single-source report analysis, indicator enrichment
teaching_note: Synthetic input R1§2 says 'review is required before a seminar memo is shared'; the question asks whether review is required. The bounded result is yes for this fictional rule, citing R1§2; a follow-up asking whether it is legally enforceable has no supporting material and receives abstain, not an embellished legal conclusion.
title: Application: Single-source report analysis, indicator enrichment

raw: *Code Archetype*: LangChain LCEL ReAct agent with tool calling
teaching_note: The framework-neutral archetype has propose, preflight, read and assess states, with a terminal unsupported state. An advertised tool is merely a capability: preflight rejects anything outside the approved packet even when the generated arguments are schema-valid; the inherited framework name is not an API-version guarantee.
title: Code Archetype: LangChain LCEL ReAct agent with tool calling

raw: **Pattern 2: The Reflection Agent** — Self-evaluation after each action step[^139]
teaching_note: The Reflection and Bias-Check Agent revises a draft against explicit criteria, unlike Pattern 1's next-observation loop. Feedback and episodic memory can change subsequent behavior, but self-critique is not an independent source and cannot automatically raise confidence. [@scholarly_shinn_2023_reflexion]
title: Pattern 2: The Reflection Agent — Self-evaluation after each action step

raw: *Methods*: Internal scoring, critic models, trajectory validation
teaching_note: Use a rubric with passage support, source currency and preserved alternatives; allow at most one critique and one revision in this toy exercise. A stylistic rewrite that changes 'likely' to 'certain' without new evidence fails the rubric even if a critic assigns it a higher internal score.
title: Methods: Internal scoring, critic models, trajectory validation

raw: *Application*: OSINT verification loop, analytic bias detection
teaching_note: A synthetic draft says 'three independent sources require review'; the critic traces all three to R1. The completed revision says 'one originating rule, reproduced in three records, requires review'; the wording-only alternative 'three reliable sources' is rejected because it preserves the independence error.
title: Application: OSINT verification loop, analytic bias detection

raw: *Code Archetype*: LangGraph state machine with reflexion node
teaching_note: The state contract retains draft version, rubric failures, cited evidence and revision count; only a substantive correction closes a failure. If the source remains unavailable at the iteration cap, return the unresolved claim to a human rather than looping or silently accepting the latest prose.
title: Code Archetype: LangGraph state machine with reflexion node

raw: **Pattern 3: The Tool-Forager** — Agent with comprehensive external tool access[^144]
teaching_note: The safe identity is Tool-Allowlist Research Assistant: select among a small authorized set, not comprehensive external access. Protocol discovery describes available tools; only the human/host scope grants permission for a particular resource and action. [@official_model_context_protocol_specification]
title: Pattern 3: The Tool-Forager — Agent with comprehensive external tool access

raw: *Methods*: Function calling, JSON schema execution, grounded output
teaching_note: Check tool name, argument types, resource membership, scope expiry and budget separately. JSON schema validity establishes structure, not authorization or truth; tool-returned text remains evidence to inspect rather than a new instruction channel.
title: Methods: Function calling, JSON schema execution, grounded output

raw: *Application*: Multi-source data harvesting, real-time collection
teaching_note: In the offline fixture, local_read(record='R1') is permitted under packet P1; local_read(record='outside-P1') is well-formed but denied. The expected result is one permitted observation and one denial with no broader-connector fallback; the denial does not license 'harvesting' elsewhere.
title: Application: Multi-source data harvesting, real-time collection

raw: *Code Archetype*: OpenAI function calling with Recon-ng, Shodan, STIX tools
teaching_note: Replace operational connectors in the inherited motif with an in-memory local-record adapter for teaching. The adapter exposes only supplied record IDs and returns a typed allow/deny result before reading; no scanner, network lookup, credentials or external collection is part of this archetype.
title: Code Archetype: OpenAI function calling with Recon-ng, Shodan, STIX tools

raw: **Pattern 4: The Planner-Executor** — Long-horizon task decomposition[^139][^145]
teaching_note: The Governed Planner-Executor separates dependency design from execution authority. A plan proposes tasks and expected artifacts; each execution still requires current permission, and a longer plan does not enlarge scope. [@scholarly_anthropic_building_effective_agents]
title: Pattern 4: The Planner-Executor — Long-horizon task decomposition

raw: *Methods*: Chain-of-thought with memory rehydration, execution DAGs
teaching_note: Use a dependency graph: T1 classify source versions → status table; T2 group origins → lineage table; T3 compare claims requires both tables; T4 draft requires T3 and a review checkpoint. Rehydrated memory must cite its checkpoint and accepted source IDs rather than filling missing prerequisites from a plausible recollection.
title: Methods: Chain-of-thought with memory rehydration, execution DAGs

raw: *Application*: Multi-phase operation planning, collection management
teaching_note: Synthetic T1 finishes but T2 returns 'origin of R4 unknown'; T3 must not label R4 independent. The completed decision is pause the independence claim, draft only the supported policy wording with that caveat, and request a local lineage review rather than collect outside the packet.
title: Application: Multi-phase operation planning, collection management

raw: *Code Archetype*: LangGraph DAG flow with priority queues
teaching_note: A task record needs prerequisites, output artifact/version and pending/completed/failed/cancelled state; queue priority never overrides a failed prerequisite. On budget exhaustion, cancel pending descendants and hand off the partial graph explicitly instead of claiming the planned outcome occurred.
title: Code Archetype: LangGraph DAG flow with priority queues

raw: **Pattern 5: The Parallel Collector** — Concurrent multi-source collection[^144]
teaching_note: The Parallel Source-Corroboration Agent compares supplied evidence concurrently; concurrency is a scheduling property, not corroboration. Count documents, originating evidence families and reviewers separately, because agreeing agents may all consume the same origin. [@official_odni_icd_206]
title: Pattern 5: The Parallel Collector — Concurrent multi-source collection

raw: *Methods*: Concurrent tool invocation, aggregation, deduplication
teaching_note: Build an origin graph before aggregation: R2 is a mirror of R1; R4 paraphrases R1; R6 is a separately created local record. The graph has four documents but two origin families; semantic similarity alone cannot prove or disprove that dependency, so retain uncertain lineage as unknown.
title: Methods: Concurrent tool invocation, aggregation, deduplication

raw: *Application*: Simultaneous OSINT/SIGINT metadata collection
teaching_note: In a synthetic packet, R1/R2/R4 say 'review required' and independent R6 records an exception. The result is one supporting family plus one contrary family, not a 3–1 majority; preserve the exception and ask whether its date and scope apply before making a universal claim. This is offline source comparison, not SIGINT collection.
title: Application: Simultaneous OSINT/SIGINT metadata collection

raw: *Code Archetype*: CrewAI parallel task execution with consensus scoring
teaching_note: Each parallel worker returns source IDs, passages, origin links and unresolved contradictions, not just a vote. Merge by evidence family and keep dissent; an unavailable worker yields an incomplete branch, never an invented agreeing result or permission to expand collection.
title: Code Archetype: CrewAI parallel task execution with consensus scoring

raw: **Pattern 6: The Multi-Agent Crew** — Specialized agents in collaborative formation[^139][^146]
teaching_note: The Role-Separated Review Crew makes responsibilities inspectable through different input/output contracts. Roles are organizational boundaries, not independent evidence or automatically isolated security principals; interoperability does not supply these guarantees. [@official_agent2agent_protocol_specification]
title: Pattern 6: The Multi-Agent Crew — Specialized agents in collaborative formation

raw: *Methods*: Planner + Retriever + Executor + Validator + Reporter roles
teaching_note: Planner returns task IDs and dependencies; retriever returns original passage IDs; the local executor performs only approved record transformations; validator checks originals and marks support; reporter consumes accepted claims plus caveats. No role shares credentials or approval power by implication, and the validator must report unavailable originals rather than accept the retriever's assertion.
title: Methods: Planner + Retriever + Executor + Validator + Reporter roles

raw: *Application*: All-source intelligence fusion; Red/Blue Cell simulation
teaching_note: Synthetic retriever output cites R3 as current, but the validator reopens R3 and finds 'draft, superseded'. The reporter removes the currency claim and retains R3 only as historical contradiction; if R1 cannot be opened, the final packet says current rule unresolved rather than merging the crew's confident summaries.
title: Application: All-source intelligence fusion; Red/Blue Cell simulation

raw: *Code Archetype*: CrewAI role-based crew with hierarchical process manager
teaching_note: Represent role handoffs as typed local records with parent task, input version and accepted output IDs. Reject a reporter output that introduces an uncited claim; the manager checks completeness of contracts, not merely whether every role emitted fluent text.
title: Code Archetype: CrewAI role-based crew with hierarchical process manager

raw: **Pattern 7: The Debate Agent** — Adversarial multi-agent reasoning[^147]
teaching_note: The Competing-Hypotheses Debate Agent contrasts explanations against evidence, rather than selecting the most persuasive speaker. Debate is a proposed classroom comparison method, not a demonstrated cure for bias; preserve dissent when the evidence cannot discriminate. [@official_odni_icd_203; @official_cia_tradecraft_primer]
title: Pattern 7: The Debate Agent — Adversarial multi-agent reasoning

raw: *Methods*: Devil's Advocacy automation, competing hypotheses generation
teaching_note: For a fictional missing library notice, compare H1 scheduled maintenance, H2 accidental publication failure and H3 deliberate removal without inferring a culprit. Mark each observation's consistency with all three and ask which observation would actually distinguish them; an outage alone fits every hypothesis and has low diagnostic value.
title: Methods: Devil's Advocacy automation, competing hypotheses generation

raw: *Application*: Automated Analysis of Competing Hypotheses (ACH)
teaching_note: Input E1 is a missing page and E2 a dated maintenance notice covering the same interval. The bounded result favors maintenance over an unsupported hostile explanation but does not eliminate publication error; if E2's date proves stale, withdraw that preference and return unresolved. Evidence consistency is not a calibrated posterior probability.
title: Application: Automated Analysis of Competing Hypotheses (ACH)

raw: *Code Archetype*: AutoGen two-agent debate pattern with judge agent
teaching_note: A judge record scores passage support, treatment of disconfirming evidence and discriminatory value, never rhetorical confidence or majority agreement. Have a reviewer inspect originals before seeing peers' conclusions in one comparison; record this as a proposed bias-control exercise, not a guarantee of independence.
title: Code Archetype: AutoGen two-agent debate pattern with judge agent

raw: **Pattern 8: The RAG-Operator** — Retrieval-Augmented Generation over intelligence corpora[^148]
teaching_note: The Provenance-Bound Retrieval Operator retrieves relevant passages from a fixed approved corpus and binds claims to them. Retrieval rank, citation presence and source instructions are not truth or authority; indirect-injection research motivates this distinction without validating a complete defense. [@scholarly_greshake_2023_indirect_prompt_injection]
title: Pattern 8: The RAG-Operator — Retrieval-Augmented Generation over intelligence corpora

raw: *Methods*: Dense vector retrieval, hybrid BM25+dense, re-ranking
teaching_note: Lexical retrieval matches terms, dense retrieval matches learned representations, and reranking reorders candidates; none establishes entailment. Retain query, corpus version, passage IDs and rejected candidates so a reviewer can distinguish retrieval failure from a generator adding an unsupported claim.
title: Methods: Dense vector retrieval, hybrid BM25+dense, re-ranking

raw: *Application*: All-source fusion from live document collections
teaching_note: In offline corpus P1, R1§2 answers the review question; R5 contains relevant commentary plus an embedded direction to send the ledger. Extract the commentary only as evidence, deny the direction as outside scope, and answer a question about enforcement penalties with 'not in P1'; relevance does not justify following source-carried instructions.
title: Application: All-source fusion from live document collections

raw: *Code Archetype*: LangChain RAG with Chroma/Pinecone over STIX feeds
teaching_note: The educational archetype is a local passage-index lookup followed by a claim-to-passage check, not a live-feed client. Keep retrieved bytes and derived notes distinct, and quarantine suspect notes before they enter accepted memory; cleaning text or displaying a warning is not a complete security boundary.
title: Code Archetype: LangChain RAG with Chroma/Pinecone over STIX feeds

raw: **Pattern 9: The Memory-State Machine** — Persistent episodic memory agent[^138]
teaching_note: The Evidence-Memory State Machine tracks what may be reused and why, rather than treating persistence as knowledge. A stored summary remains a derived assertion with dependencies, not a new independent source or an enduring approval. [@official_cisa_ai_data_security_best_practices]
title: Pattern 9: The Memory-State Machine — Persistent episodic memory agent

raw: *Methods*: Episodic memory write/read, consolidation, attention-weighted retrieval
teaching_note: Use proposed → accepted → superseded or quarantined states, each carrying origin, corpus version and reviewer. Consolidation may shorten text but must preserve claim dependencies and uncertainty; attention or retrieval weight is not an acceptance decision.
title: Methods: Episodic memory write/read, consolidation, attention-weighted retrieval

raw: *Application*: Long-term asset tracking, longitudinal pattern-of-life analysis
teaching_note: The safe synthetic application follows document revisions, not people: M1 summarizes draft R3 as current; correction R1 identifies R3 as superseded. Mark M1 superseded, invalidate dependent claim C1 and rebuild C2 from R1 with a correction link; do not merely append R1 while leaving M1 retrievable as accepted.
title: Application: Long-term asset tracking, longitudinal pattern-of-life analysis

raw: *Code Archetype*: LangGraph with PostgreSQL episodic memory and mem0/MemGPT
teaching_note: A local state table can demonstrate transition guards: only accepted records are eligible for answer support, while rejected and quarantined records remain available for audit. Recovery restores a named pre-incident checkpoint and revalidates affected dependencies; changing database products does not itself supply this policy.
title: Code Archetype: LangGraph with PostgreSQL episodic memory and mem0/MemGPT

raw: **Pattern 10: The Control Plane Agent** — Modular tool routing through single interface[^145]
teaching_note: The Permissioned Control Plane Agent centralizes routing decisions, not unrestricted powers. One meta-tool can conceal many subtools, so authorization must follow the resolved operation and resource rather than approving the wrapper name alone. [@official_model_context_protocol_security_best_practices]
title: Pattern 10: The Control Plane Agent — Modular tool routing through single interface

raw: *Methods*: "Control Plane as a Tool" abstraction, modular routing logic
teaching_note: Effective permission is the intersection of human task scope, child grant, tool/resource policy and remaining budget; any failed condition denies the request. Scope expiry and cancellation are separate from schema validation, and confidence is never an authorization input.
title: Methods: "Control Plane as a Tool" abstraction, modular routing logic

raw: *Application*: Scalable multi-source collection with single interface
teaching_note: Synthetic route('read','R1') passes packet membership and one remaining read; route('send','ledger') fails the human scope even though the wrapper accepts both verbs. After the read consumes the budget, a second read is denied as exhausted; the completed record distinguishes scope denial from budget denial without executing either denied action.
title: Application: Scalable multi-source collection with single interface

raw: *Code Archetype*: FastAPI meta-tool endpoint wrapping N sub-tools
teaching_note: Model the wrapper as an offline dispatch table with a preflight decision before each local adapter. Preserve the resolved subtool and policy version in the event record; a wrapper's successful response must not conceal a denied sub-operation or imply that all N operations were approved.
title: Code Archetype: FastAPI meta-tool endpoint wrapping N sub-tools

raw: **Pattern 11: The Surveillance Agent** — Continuous monitoring and alerting
teaching_note: The safe Monitoring-Governance Tabletop Agent reviews supplied toy asset-health events, never people or live infrastructure. Monitoring compares observations with a declared baseline; absence of a report is unknown, not a normal reading or proof of concealment.
title: Pattern 11: The Surveillance Agent — Continuous monitoring and alerting

raw: *Methods*: Scheduled polling, anomaly detection, threshold alerting
teaching_note: Define the classroom baseline as 10–20 fictional units and flag values above 20 for review, not for automatic intervention. Record measurement validity and missingness before thresholding; a threshold is an author-chosen rule for this fixture, not an empirically optimal detector.
title: Methods: Scheduled polling, anomaly detection, threshold alerting

raw: *Application*: Persistent target monitoring, dark web alerting, infrastructure tracking
teaching_note: Supplied events are 15, 28 and missing; metadata says the 28 reading used a different unit. The completed disposition is normal-in-fixture for 15, invalid-comparison/review for 28 and unknown for missing, with no automated response; conversion evidence would be needed before calling 28 a true anomaly.
title: Application: Persistent target monitoring, dark web alerting, infrastructure tracking

raw: *Code Archetype*: n8n or LangGraph cron-triggered agent with Shodan/SpiderFoot APIs
teaching_note: Use a finite in-memory event list and emit a local review queue; do not schedule polling or invoke the inherited operational APIs. A run stops at the list boundary or invalid metadata, and records whether an apparent alert was a unit mismatch rather than silently counting it as detector success.
title: Code Archetype: n8n or LangGraph cron-triggered agent with Shodan/SpiderFoot APIs

raw: **Pattern 12: The Red Team Agent** — Adversarial attack simulation[^147]
teaching_note: The Control-Coverage Critique Agent challenges claims about a control using supplied benign scenarios and review evidence, not attack execution. A taxonomy label organizes a failure mode; it does not demonstrate coverage or effectiveness. [@official_mitre_atlas; @official_cisa_ai_red_teaming_tev]
title: Pattern 12: The Red Team Agent — Adversarial attack simulation

raw: *Methods*: Adversarial prompt generation, attack-tree traversal, kill chain simulation
teaching_note: Construct the review chain scenario → claimed control → observable decision record → uncovered failure → responsible remediation owner. Use prewritten non-executable embedded-direction records; do not generate operational payloads or infer that a checked threat-category box means the scenario was tested.
title: Methods: Adversarial prompt generation, attack-tree traversal, kill chain simulation

raw: *Application*: Penetration testing automation, vulnerability discovery
teaching_note: A synthetic control claim says 'warnings prevent source instructions'; the supplied trace shows the warning, no outbound action, but a contaminated accepted summary. The bounded finding is incomplete coverage of memory contamination, assigned to the memory-policy owner; no claim about real penetration or vulnerability prevalence follows.
title: Application: Penetration testing automation, vulnerability discovery

raw: *Code Archetype*: AutoGen code execution agent with MITRE ATT&CK tool plugin
teaching_note: The safe archetype validates a static control-evidence matrix and marks absent observations 'not demonstrated'. Retest means checking a new supplied trace against the same criterion; neither a plugin name nor an agent-generated verdict substitutes for the missing observation.
title: Code Archetype: AutoGen code execution agent with MITRE ATT&CK tool plugin

raw: **Pattern 13: The Cover Story Generator** — Legend and cover document creation
teaching_note: The Identity-and-Provenance Fiction Audit examines pre-supplied fictional artifacts for internal provenance consistency; it creates no identity, cover document or operational persona. Distinguish a signature's validity, the identity asserted by its issuer and the truth of the artifact's claims. [@official_c2pa_specifications; @official_w3c_vc_data_integrity]
title: Pattern 13: The Cover Story Generator — Legend and cover document creation

raw: *Methods*: Persona generation, document synthesis, consistency checking
teaching_note: Compare supplied issuance dates, issuer IDs and declared derivation links without inventing missing credentials. A valid signature can establish a particular integrity relationship under a trust model, but it does not make every statement true; an absent credential is inconclusive, not proof of deception.
title: Methods: Persona generation, document synthesis, consistency checking

raw: *Application*: NOC legend maintenance, sock puppet operational security
teaching_note: Fictional artifact A claims derivation from B dated day 4 although A is dated day 2. Record the temporal inconsistency and possible date-entry error, and return 'provenance unresolved'; do not infer a real person's identity or intent, repair the fiction, or generate replacement documents.
title: Application: NOC legend maintenance, sock puppet operational security

raw: *Code Archetype*: GPT-4o with structured output schemas for persona consistency
teaching_note: A local consistency checker emits artifact ID, conflicting fields, alternative explanation and evidence-needed status. Its schema limits the output to an audit record; it neither manufactures credentials nor claims cryptographic verification from a model's textual impression.
title: Code Archetype: GPT-4o with structured output schemas for persona consistency

raw: **Pattern 14: The Deception Detector** — Verification and source reliability agent
teaching_note: The Source-Reliability Verification Agent evaluates separate dimensions instead of producing a universal deception score. Source reliability concerns a source's relevant record, content credibility concerns this assertion, and authenticity, relevance and origin independence require their own evidence. [@official_odni_icd_203; @official_odni_icd_206]
title: Pattern 14: The Deception Detector — Verification and source reliability agent

raw: *Methods*: Cross-source triangulation, metadata analysis, deepfake detection API calls
teaching_note: Check the artifact's provenance separately from whether its content is supported and current. A detector output is another fallible observation with a version and task context, not a verdict on intent; no detector API is called in this classroom exercise.
title: Methods: Cross-source triangulation, metadata analysis, deepfake detection API calls

raw: *Application*: Source vetting, product validation, disinformation identification
teaching_note: A synthetic authentic signed draft says review is optional, while a later current rule says required. The result is 'authentic historical draft, not current support', not 'forgery' or 'deception detected'; if version order is unknown, retain both claims and abstain on the current rule.
title: Application: Source vetting, product validation, disinformation identification

raw: *Code Archetype*: LangChain agent with Hive Moderation, Sightengine, C2PA APIs
teaching_note: The offline archetype returns a dimensioned record: authenticity evidence, claim support, date relevance, origin dependency and unresolved alternatives. A missing dimension remains unknown instead of being collapsed into a confident binary label; provenance standards do not establish factual truth. [@official_c2pa_specifications]
title: Code Archetype: LangChain agent with Hive Moderation, Sightengine, C2PA APIs

raw: **Pattern 15: The Analyst in the Loop** — Human-in-the-loop (HITL) intelligence agent[^4]
teaching_note: The Analyst-in-the-Loop Review Agent routes consequential decisions to an accountable owner before the relevant transition. Review must be resourced and actionable; a human name in a diagram and high model confidence do not create approval. [@official_canada_agentic_ai_guide]
title: Pattern 15: The Analyst in the Loop — Human-in-the-loop (HITL) intelligence agent

raw: *Methods*: Interrupt-and-query, confidence-gated human escalation
teaching_note: The gate asks for approve/revise/deny on an exact artifact version, proposed action, destination, evidence/caveats and expiry. Scope, rights and irreversibility gates apply regardless of confidence; unavailable or expired ownership means hold, not implicit consent.
title: Methods: Interrupt-and-query, confidence-gated human escalation

raw: *Application*: Supervised analysis; compliance-constrained environments
teaching_note: Synthetic request A1 asks reviewer Instructor-A to accept draft D1-v2 for local seminar review only until session end; the decision is revise because R3 is mislabeled current. D1-v3 corrects the label but requires a new decision; neither approval would authorize excluded external sharing, and a claimed 99% confidence changes nothing.
title: Application: Supervised analysis; compliance-constrained environments

raw: *Code Archetype*: LangGraph with human_approval node and async interrupt handlers
teaching_note: A resumable approval state stores request ID, owner, artifact version, exact action and decision expiry. Before resuming, compare all bound fields; a changed draft, action, destination or owner pauses the transition for a fresh decision rather than replaying a stale approval.
title: Code Archetype: LangGraph with human_approval node and async interrupt handlers

raw: **Pattern 16: The Cyber Sentinel** — Autonomous threat intelligence and response[^149][^150]
teaching_note: The SOC Tabletop Triage Agent interprets fabricated alert records and recommends local review, not autonomous response. An observable is a recorded property, an indicator is an analytic assertion useful under stated conditions, and an incident requires contextual assessment; none follows automatically from the others. [@official_oasis_stix_21]
title: Pattern 16: The Cyber Sentinel — Autonomous threat intelligence and response

raw: *Methods*: SIEM integration, SOAR automation, ATT&CK technique mapping
teaching_note: Map only behavior actually described by the supplied record and retain uncertainty when the taxonomy requires missing context. An ATT&CK match is a classification aid, not attribution, severity or proof of compromise; the inherited NGA-style/contextual references do not validate a SOC mapping. [@official_mitre_attack_enterprise]
title: Methods: SIEM integration, SOAR automation, ATT&CK technique mapping

raw: *Application*: Autonomous SOC tier-1 triage, IOC enrichment
teaching_note: Fictional alert E1 reports three failed test logins; E2 records a scheduled local test in the same interval. The completed decision is 'review context, insufficient evidence for incident', retaining a benign test explanation and any timestamp mismatch; do not block an account, enrich a real indicator or publish anything.
title: Application: Autonomous SOC tier-1 triage, IOC enrichment

raw: *Code Archetype*: CrewAI crew with Splunk/Elastic SIEM tools and STIX/TAXII writer
teaching_note: A deterministic local adapter reads fabricated alert IDs and emits a triage card with evidence, missing context and human disposition. No SIEM access, response connector or TAXII writer is enabled; export format validity would not authorize publication or establish the claim's accuracy.
title: Code Archetype: CrewAI crew with Splunk/Elastic SIEM tools and STIX/TAXII writer

raw: **Pattern 17: The Supply Chain Inspector** — Software provenance and integrity agent
teaching_note: The Software Provenance Review Agent separates package identity, build provenance, advisory affectedness and exploitability. An SBOM is an inventory representation, not proof that every dependency is safe or that a named maintainer acted maliciously. [@official_nist_ssdf; @official_nist_sp_800_161r1]
title: Pattern 17: The Supply Chain Inspector — Software provenance and integrity agent

raw: *Methods*: SBOM parsing, dependency graph analysis, commit diff analysis
teaching_note: Compare ecosystem, namespace, version, source and build identifiers before applying an advisory's affected range. A dependency edge shows inclusion or relationship under the supplied inventory, not reachability of a vulnerable path; an unusual diff is a review cue, not evidence of intent.
title: Methods: SBOM parsing, dependency graph analysis, commit diff analysis

raw: *Application*: Open-source supply chain threat hunting (post-XZ Utils)[^76]
teaching_note: Synthetic inventory lists classroom-parser 1.2 without an ecosystem; an advisory affects a similarly named package 1.0–1.4 in ecosystem E. The result is 'identity unresolved; affectedness unknown', with a request for the supplied lockfile or provenance record; name/version resemblance does not justify 'vulnerable' or a maintainer accusation.
title: Application: Open-source supply chain threat hunting (post-XZ Utils)

raw: *Code Archetype*: Python agent with Syft/Grype SBOM tools and GitHub commit analysis
teaching_note: Use local fixture parsers returning matched, not-matched or identity-unknown with advisory and inventory versions. Preserve an unknown result rather than treating a parse failure or missing provenance as 'no vulnerabilities'; this archetype runs no package scanners or repository actions.
title: Code Archetype: Python agent with Syft/Grype SBOM tools and GitHub commit analysis

raw: **Pattern 18: The GEOINT Analyst** — Automated satellite imagery analysis
teaching_note: The GEOINT Data-Quality Audit Agent checks whether supplied synthetic image records permit comparison before interpreting apparent change. Resolution, temporal consistency and registration are distinct quality conditions; no real location, facility or order of battle is identified. [@official_iso_19157_data_quality]
title: Pattern 18: The GEOINT Analyst — Automated satellite imagery analysis

raw: *Methods*: Vision model object detection, change detection, chronolocation
teaching_note: Compare acquisition times, pixel scale, registration uncertainty and processing differences before applying a change label. A vision model's object name is a proposed interpretation, not validated ground truth, and cannot repair incompatible input geometry.
title: Methods: Vision model object detection, change detection, chronolocation

raw: *Application*: Facility monitoring, order-of-battle assessment
teaching_note: Synthetic image A has 1-unit pixels, image B has 5-unit pixels and uncertain registration of 8 units; a reported 3-unit edge shift is therefore not interpretable as physical change. The completed result is stop/inputs incompatible and request an approved comparable pair, not 'object moved' or an operational inference.
title: Application: Facility monitoring, order-of-battle assessment

raw: *Code Archetype*: GPT-4o Vision + Google Earth Engine API + LangChain agent loop

raw: **Pattern 19: The Cognitive Inoculant** — Prebunking and cognitive resilience agent[^151]
teaching_note: The Cognitive-Resilience Education Agent presents an opt-in transparent media-literacy lesson, not population targeting or covert persuasion. Distinguish recognition/discernment on a study task from durable behavior change and from efficacy of agent-delivered teaching; practitioner guidance alone cannot establish those transfers. [@scholarly_roozenbeek_2022_psychological_inoculation]
title: Pattern 19: The Cognitive Inoculant — Prebunking and cognitive resilience agent

raw: *Methods*: Manipulation technique detection, inoculation content generation, user adaptation
teaching_note: A proposed micro-lesson explains false dilemmas with a benign fictional sentence, then asks for an explanation on an unseen item. Use explicit consent and fixed classroom materials; do not infer vulnerabilities, profile learners or adapt influence tactics to personal traits.
title: Methods: Manipulation technique detection, inoculation content generation, user adaptation

raw: *Application*: Population-scale cognitive security intervention delivery[^152]
teaching_note: Teaching item: 'Either our library changes its logo or it opposes reading' excludes other choices; an illustrative transfer item, 'Either extend opening hours or abandon students', repeats that false-dilemma structure. The expected answer identifies the excluded alternatives, not merely the favored policy; a learner who only labels disagreement has not shown the target skill. This is a published answer-key illustration, not a genuine held-out evaluation or an observed learner outcome; actual evaluation needs new isolated items and cannot establish population effects from this example.
title: Application: Population-scale cognitive security intervention delivery

raw: **Pattern 20: The Hierarchical Command** — Orchestrator-subagent architecture[^139][^137]
teaching_note: The Hierarchical Curriculum Orchestrator coordinates bounded child contracts and aggregates evidence dependencies, not obedience-based authority. A parent cannot delegate powers it lacks, and child agreement is not independent evidence. [@official_canada_agentic_ai_guide; @official_agent2agent_protocol_specification]
title: Pattern 20: The Hierarchical Command — Orchestrator-subagent architecture

raw: *Methods*: Goal decomposition, subagent delegation, output aggregation, failure recovery
teaching_note: Root T0 grants C1 only source-status review of R1/R3 and C2 only lineage review of R2/R4, expiring at checkpoint K1; neither may redelegate. Each returns input version, passages, accepted claims and pending/failed work, so aggregation can distinguish a missing branch from a negative finding.
title: Methods: Goal decomposition, subagent delegation, output aggregation, failure recovery

raw: *Application*: Complex multi-domain operations with role separation
teaching_note: In the synthetic handoff, C1 completes but C2 consumes a suspect note and is cancelled; T0 marks lineage incomplete, quarantines C2's descendants and drafts only source-status findings. The next owner receives checkpoint K0, rejected-note IDs and pending C2 review, not a fabricated complete synthesis; resume requires a clean local rerun and new owner acceptance.
title: Application: Complex multi-domain operations with role separation

raw: *Code Archetype*: LangGraph supervisor pattern with specialized subagent nodes
teaching_note: The supervisor stores a delegation tree, scope expiry, cancellation state and claim-to-child/source manifest; it rejects unsupported additions at merge time. Suspect memory may propagate through handoffs, so recovery excludes affected derived notes rather than trusting a fresh agent with the same contaminated context; this is a proposed control, not demonstrated immunity. [@scholarly_prompt_infection_multi_agent]
